purpose: Adds Host Google Fonts Locally feature that detects Google Fonts from fonts.googleapis.com, downloads CSS and woff2 files, caches them under wp-content/cache/wppo/fonts/, and rewrites URLs to local paths with font-display: swap applied.
riskRationale: All 5 previously reported issues (critical v1→v2 URL bug, race condition, overly broad cache purge, duplicate instances, inconsistent test mock) have been correctly resolved. One important edge case (empty file validation for failed downloads) and one minor issue (unused constant) remain — both are straightforward fixes with no security or breaking concerns.

text: The implementation follows the codebase's established patterns (singleton instance injected into Cache via setter, style_loader_tag interception at priority 9 before minification, buffer-level @import interception). All 5 previously reported issues have been fixed. One important edge case around empty downloaded font files and one minor unused constant remain. The JS component and tests are consistent with existing patterns.

reasoning: An important edge case persists: if the remote Google Fonts server returns 200 with an empty/truncated body, a 0-byte woff2 file is cached permanently via atomic rename, silently breaking @font-face rendering on the frontend until manual cache clear. The fix is a simple filesize() guard after download.

message: Atomic write pattern with temp-file-then-rename (wp_rand suffix, cleanup on failure) correctly resolves the concurrent download race condition for font files.
style_loader_tag filter at priority 9 correctly executes before minify_css at priority 10, ensuring Google Fonts URLs are rewritten to local paths before CSS minification.
Font cache invalidation is scoped to only the setting toggle (hostGoogleFontsLocally), not triggered on every full cache purge — preventing unnecessary re-downloads.
normalized_google_fonts_url() correctly keeps v1 API URLs on the /css endpoint instead of attempting risky v1-to-v2 format conversion, avoiding silently broken multi-weight font configurations.

No validation that the downloaded font file is non-empty. If the remote server returns 200 with an empty or truncated body (transient error, early connection close), the empty temp file is renamed to the destination and cached permanently. file_exists() returns true for 0-byte files, so subsequent page loads reference an empty woff2 file, silently breaking @font-face rendering on the frontend until manual cache clear.
suggestion: Add filesize() validation after the HTTP response check. Delete the temp file and return false if the file is empty or missing.

message: The private constant FONTS_API ('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2') is defined but never referenced anywhere in the class. After the fix to keep v1 URLs on the /css endpoint, this constant became dead code. While harmless, it misleads maintainers into thinking the class uses the v2 API.

The Google Fonts buffer-level interception (process_buffer) runs only inside process_buffer_only(), which executes only when the page cache is enabled. When enableCache is false but hostGoogleFontsLocally is on, @import in <style> tags and inline <link> patterns in templates are not intercepted. The style_loader_tag filter handles enqueued fonts (the common case), so this is a limited gap.
suggestion: Add Google Fonts buffer processing to the standalone output buffer paths (process_used_css_only / start_used_css_buffer) when hostGoogleFontsLocally is enabled and enableCache is disabled.
